h1: When does a residential project trigger a Newton Stormwater Management Permit?
title: Newton Stormwater Permits: Land Disturbance and Impervious Area
description: Review the published Newton land-disturbance and new-impervious-area thresholds that can trigger stormwater review.
short_answer: Newton's stormwater ordinance requires a permit before certain land-disturbance projects that could disturb more than 5,000 square feet. It also identifies residential projects creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as a minor stormwater-review category. Other triggers include certain retaining walls and trench excavation requiring dewatering.

facts.text: Newton's ordinance lists projects that will or could disturb more than 5,000 square feet of land as requiring a stormwater management and erosion control permit.
The ordinance lists residential development or redevelopment creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as a minor stormwater management category.

qa.q: Can a small residential project trigger stormwater review even when it disturbs less than 5,000 square feet?
qa.a: Yes. The ordinance separately lists certain residential projects creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as a minor stormwater category.
